what: Synopsys makes software for designing chips, licenses pre-built design blocks that chipmakers put into their products, and since buying Ansys also sells simulation software for physical engineering.
customers: Semiconductor companies, cloud providers designing custom silicon, carmakers, and now engineering firms using simulation.
money: chip design, verification and manufacturing software
ready-made interface and processor blocks licensed to chipmakers
Ansys physics simulation for structures, fluids and electromagnetics
moat: Its tools and intellectual property blocks are designed into chip projects that run for years, and the industry depends on only two or three suppliers.
risks: The Ansys acquisition added about $11 billion of debt and depressed reported returns
Export restrictions limit sales to Chinese customers
Integration of a large acquisition takes management attention
Revenue is concentrated among a few very large chipmakers
opportunities: Every new AI chip design, from cloud providers and startups alike, needs its tools and blocks
Combining chip design with physical simulation lets it sell into whole-system engineering
Recurring licence revenue gives multi-year visibility
watch: Backlog growth and progress on the Ansys integration and debt reduction.
